failures.title: Peugeot DV6TED4 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Injector failure - leak-off and electrical faults
items.whatHappens: The DV6TED4's piezo injectors are the most common failure point on this engine. Injector failure manifests as rough idle, hesitation under acceleration, poor fuel economy, and difficulty starting. The injectors can fail electrically (internal solenoid issues) or mechanically (leak-off causing fuel pressure loss). Swarf contamination from fuel pump wear can also damage injectors.
items.repairVsReplace: Individual injector replacement is possible (£300-£800 per injector). However, if injector failure has caused bore wash (fuel dilution of engine oil) or cylinder damage, a replacement engine may be more cost-effective. Regular injector servicing (clean and balance) at 80,000 miles is recommended.

items.title: DPF clogging (urban use)
items.whatHappens: Like all modern diesels, the DV6TED4 suffers from DPF clogging when used predominantly for short urban trips. Symptoms include reduced power, increased fuel consumption, and warning lights. The DPF is sensitive to the 1.6 HDi's frequent regeneration cycles; urban driving prevents passive regeneration, leading to soot accumulation.
items.repairVsReplace: DPF cleaning or replacement (£400-£1,200) is a standard maintenance item. This is not an engine-replacement trigger unless neglected to the point of causing back-pressure damage or turbo failure. A DPF delete is illegal for road use in the UK.

items.title: Turbocharger failure - actuator and oil supply issues
items.whatHappens: Turbocharger failure on the DV6TED4 is typically caused by oil supply issues (blocked oil feed pipes from infrequent oil changes) or boost pressure actuator failure. Symptoms include loss of power, excessive smoke, whistling noises, and boost pressure fault codes. The variable geometry actuator is a known weak point.
items.repairVsReplace: Turbocharger replacement costs £800-£2,000. However, if turbo failure has sent debris through the engine, a full engine replacement may be necessary. Regular oil changes with the correct specification oil are critical to turbo longevity.

items.title: EGR valve clogging
items.whatHappens: The EGR valve on the DV6TED4 is prone to clogging with soot, particularly on urban-driven vehicles. Symptoms include rough idle, hesitation on acceleration, and reduced power. The EGR valve can stick open or closed, causing poor driveability and fault codes.
items.repairVsReplace: EGR valve cleaning or replacement is a standard maintenance item (£200-£600). Proactive EGR cleaning at 60,000 miles prevents more serious issues.

failures.goodYearsLine: The DV6TED4 is one of the most reliable diesel engines ever produced - it is the backbone of the European small diesel market. With strict 10,000-mile oil changes using the correct 5W-30 or 0W-30 spec oil (Ford WSS-M2C913-C/D or PSA B71 2290), regular DPF-friendly motorway driving, and proactive injector maintenance, DV6TED4 engines can exceed 200,000 miles without major failure. Later units (2012 onwards) saw improved injector durability and revised ECU calibrations to reduce DPF regen frequency.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the DV6TED4
variants.intro: The DV6TED4 is a specific engine code within the Ford-PSA DV6 family. It is the 1.6-litre turbo-diesel variant, distinguished from the DV6C (1.5-litre) that replaced it and earlier DV4 (1.4-litre) engines. Confirming your exact code is essential before ordering a replacement. Where to find your engine code: - On the engine: Stamped on a flat machined surface on the cylinder block, typically near the transmission bell housing - On the V5C registration document: Listed under vehicle details - Via VIN: Use an online decoder with your 17-character VIN Commonly confused codes - check you have the right one: - DV6C - 1.5-litre EcoBlue / BlueHDi (2015+). The successor to the DV6TED4, with improved emissions, lower fuel consumption, and a revised fuel system. NOT interchangeable. - DV4 - 1.4-litre HDi (older generation, pre-2005). Fitted to earlier Peugeot 206, Citroën C2, Ford Fiesta. Lower output and different mounting arrangement. NOT interchangeable. - DW10 - 2.0-litre HDi / TDCi (larger application). Fitted to Mondeo, 508, C5. Completely different engine architecture. NOT interchangeable. - M9R - 2.0-litre dCi (Renault-Nissan). Competitor engine, not related. - K9K - 1.5-litre dCi (Renault-Nissan). Competitor engine, not related. Why getting the right code matters: The DV6TED4 is the most common 1.6 HDi variant - it has specific ECU calibration, injector settings, and emissions equipment (DPF on most UK models). Fitting a DV6C (1.5L) into a DV6TED4 car is not a straight swap - it requires different engine mounts, fuel system components, and ECU. Always confirm your code before purchasing.

relatives.description: - the 1.4-litre HDi that preceded the DV6TED4. Fitted to earlier Peugeot 206, Citroën C2, and Ford Fiesta models. The DV4 had lower power output (68-75 hp) and a different mounting arrangement; the DV6TED4 was a significant improvement with better power, torque, and refinement.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement DV6TED4 - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: ** A used DV6TED4 can be a sensible option for lower-value host vehicles (sub-£3,000 207, Focus, C4) - and because this engine is so common, used units are plentiful. However, only purchase with documented service history and **proof of injector condition and DPF status**. Injector issues and DPF clogging are the two biggest risks; a used unit may appear fine but suffer from hidden fuel system damage. Always request a compression test and injector leak-off test before committing to any used purchase. See used engine guide
options.href: /LINK PENDING - page not in current inventory

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: ** For most DV6TED4 owners, a reconditioned unit is the sweet spot. A proper recon addresses the injectors (reconditioned or new), timing belt (if applicable), water pump, and includes a full gasket set. Crucially, a reputable recon will refurbish the injectors and inspect the DPF - exactly the components that fail first on this engine. With a 12-24 month warranty, this is the low-risk option for vehicles worth £3,000+. See reconditioned engine guide
options.href: /LINK PENDING - page not in current inventory

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: ** A full rebuild of the DV6TED4 is only justified for high-value examples (low-mileage 308, well-specced C4, Focus) where the vehicle's value comfortably exceeds the rebuild cost. A quality rebuild should include new injectors, timing components, turbo inspection, and a full cylinder head assessment. Given the DV6TED4's widespread availability, a rebuild is rarely cost-effective compared to a quality reconditioned unit. See rebuilt engine guide
options.href: /LINK PENDING - page not in current inventory

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: ** All replacement options can be supplied and fitted through our network of vetted UK Peugeot-Citroën-Ford diesel specialists - with warranties that follow the engine, not just the car. See supply & fit
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: ** The DV6TED4 typically sits in vehicles worth £800-£8,000 (207, Focus, C4, 308, DS3). A reconditioned DV6TED4 at £1,300-£1,800 represents 16-225% of vehicle value - **a critical financial consideration**. For sub-£2,000 examples, a used engine from £450-£900 is the only financially sensible route, but only with thorough injector and DPF inspection. For vehicles worth £4,000+, a reconditioned unit is generally viable and offers peace of mind with warranty. Always evaluate the rest of the vehicle before committing - a £1,500 engine in a £1,500 car with a failing clutch, DPF, and worn suspension is rarely the right decision.

items.question: What are the most common problems with the DV6TED4 engine?
items.answer: The DV6TED4's most documented issues are: (1) injector failure - rough idle, hesitation, poor fuel economy; (2) DPF clogging in urban use; (3) turbocharger failure - often caused by oil supply issues; (4) EGR valve clogging. Regular oil changes with 5W-30 or 0W-30 spec oil are critical for turbo longevity. The DV6TED4 is considered one of the most reliable diesel engines ever produced.

items.question: How do I know if my car has the DV6TED4 engine and not another variant?
items.answer: The DV6TED4 engine code is stamped on the cylinder block - look for a flat machined surface near the transmission bell housing, typically on the front or side of the block. The code also appears on the V5C registration document and can be confirmed via the vehicle's VIN using an online decoder. The DV6TED4 is a 1.6-litre (1,560 cc) turbo-diesel with common-rail injection. It is often confused with the DV6C (1.5-litre BlueHDi) - physically similar but different displacement and emissions equipment. Ford, Peugeot, Citroën, Volvo, Mazda and Mini all use the same engine with different badging.

items.question: How long does a DV6TED4 engine last?
items.answer: With proper maintenance, the DV6TED4 can exceed 200,000 miles (≈320,000 km) and some well-maintained examples have reached 300,000+ miles. The engine's longevity is highly dependent on oil change frequency - the recommended interval is 10,000 miles (16,000 km) or annually, using 5W-30 or 0W-30 spec oil (Ford WSS-M2C913-C/D or PSA B71 2290). Regular injector servicing at 80,000 miles prevents fuel system damage. Motorway driving for DPF regeneration is essential for urban vehicles. The DV6TED4 is considered one of the most durable small diesel engines ever built.
